newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DGB sees small Feb jobless change.
newsitem.headline: German DGB sees small Feb jobless change.

text.p: The Federation of German Trade Unions (DGB) said on Monday there were no signs that data to be released this week show the number of Germans out of work hit a new record of 4.8 million in February.

DGB deputy president Ursula Engelen-Kefer told a DGB congress in Duesseldorf that she expected only a slight change in the jobless figures, disputing reports unemployment rose to 4.8 million from 4.66 million in January.
The Federal Labour Office will release February unemployment data on Thursday.

Germany's mass daily Bild newspaper has reported that unemployment rose again to 4.8 million last month, setting yet another post-war record as German unemployment continues to rise to levels not seen since the turbulent 1930s.
But Engelen-Kefer said mild weather conditions had improved conditions for the key building sector and for this reason the DGB expected only a slight change in the February data.
Bernhard Jagoda, president of the Labour Office, has urged Chancellor Helmut Kohl's government to introduce a jobs programme aimed at improving conditions for investment.
But Labour Minister Norbert Bluem said that the government alone cannot ensure that new jobs are created. In the end it was up to industry to hire people.
